clue.text: Player shooting but producing an own goal

parts.note: a back is a defensive player in football or hockey
shooting a gun is firing it

explanation.surface: A footballer shoots but puts the ball into his own net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player shooting' reads as one footballer in action; it splits into a positional player and the act of shooting.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan that backfires rebounds on its maker, just as an own goal scores against oneself.

clue.text: Cry over onion here?

indicators.note: in a down clue, over signals that the word for cry is turned upside down

parts.note: to blub is to cry, informally

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether this is the place to weep over an onion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here?' is a playful link: onions make you cry, and this is where you'd find one.
explanation.definitionFit: An onion is a vegetable that grows as a bulb, an example of the type.

clue.text: Find guilty new vicar in bed

indicators.note: the new vicar is placed inside the word for bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A scandal: a newly appointed vicar caught in bed and found guilty.
explanation.definitionFit: To convict someone is to declare them guilty in court, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Nice meals that are bland may benefit from this

definitions.text: Nice meals that are bland may benefit from this

parts.words: Nice meals that are bland may benefit from this
parts.note: Nice is the city on the Riviera, so dishes there would get a condiment from that country to liven them up

explanation.surface: Advice that bland meals could do with a little something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' at the start of the sentence hides its capital: it is the French city, not 'pleasant'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild Dijon-style mustard from France is a condiment that adds flavour to bland food.

clue.text: Messenger carrying name in letter to king

indicators.note: the abbreviation for name goes inside the word for letter

parts.note: a rune is a letter of an ancient Germanic alphabet
R (Rex) is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A courier bears a letter addressed to the king, with a name inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner is someone who carries messages, as in a battlefield or office runner.

clue.text: A late swallow

parts.note: not a bird arriving late in the year but a drink swallowed at the end of the evening

explanation.surface: A swallow that turns up late in the season.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightcap is an alcoholic drink taken just before going to bed.

clue.text: A mountain of rubber gloves

indicators.note: the answer is made of letters running across the words rubber gloves

explanation.surface: A huge heap of rubber gloves.
explanation.definitionFit: Berg means mountain in German and Afrikaans, and is short for an iceberg, a floating mountain of ice.

clue.text: Wrought Hinge Co. is sending back imitations

indicators.note: wrought means worked or shaped, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A firm called Hinge Co. returns copies of its products.
explanation.definitionFit: Echoing is sound bouncing back as a copy of itself, so it sends back imitations.

clue.text: Drive rig, taking a turn around North Dakota

parts.note: a rig-out or get-up is an outfit

indicators.note: a turn wraps around the abbreviation for North Dakota

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game
ND is the US postal abbreviation for North Dakota

explanation.surface: Instructions for steering a truck through a turn round North Dakota.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' and 'rig' suggest trucks; drive is energy and rig is clothing. 'taking' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive in the sense of energy and ambition is what get-up-and-go means.

clue.text: Light plane losing wings running into bird

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its first and last letters, which are dropped

parts.note: a plane is an aircraft, with wings
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: An aircraft clips its wings on a bird and crashes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running into' joins the shortened plane to the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a portable lamp, so a type of light.

clue.text: Comfortable about stolen report

indicators.note: about signals the word for comfortable is turned round

parts.note: snug means cosy and comfortable
hot goods are stolen ones

explanation.surface: A fence feels at ease about a report on stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is a loud bang, such as the sound of a gun being fired.

clue.text: Track featuring The White Cliffs of Dover

definitions.text: Track featuring The White Cliffs of Dover

parts.words: Track featuring The White Cliffs of Dover
parts.note: not a song title on a record but a walking route that runs along the chalk hills of south-east England to Dover

explanation.surface: A song on a record, the wartime favourite about Dover's cliffs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Track' wants to be a song, as '(There'll Be Bluebirds Over) The White Cliffs of Dover' is a famous wartime song; it is a path. This long-distance trail runs along the chalk hills of Surrey and Kent to Dover.
explanation.definitionFit: This national trail follows chalk downland across Kent and ends at the white cliffs by Dover.

clue.text: See claret run over box

indicators.note: the wine and run are placed over the box, enclosing it

parts.note: claret is red Bordeaux wine
a chest is a large box
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone is told to look at claret spilled over a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is not 'look': it is a bishop's diocese, and Winchester is a cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is a bishop's seat or diocese, and Winchester is one of the Church of England's oldest.

clue.text: Weak person losing with mischievous child

indicators.note: losing signals that the abbreviation for with is removed

parts.note: a wimp is a feeble, weak person

explanation.surface: A weakling loses out to a naughty child.
explanation.definitionFit: An imp is a little devil, used of a mischievous child.

clue.text: Swimming space, as in a large expanse of water

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters move about freely into a new order

explanation.surface: Room for a swim, like in a big stretch of water.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caspian Sea is the world's largest inland body of water, between Europe and Asia.

clue.text: Browning happened then to be addressed by Keats

definitions.meaning: the season when leaves turn brown
Keats wrote the ode To ..., which addresses the season directly

explanation.walkthrough: 'Browning' looks like the poet Robert Browning beside Keats, but it means turning brown.
explanation.definitionFit: Autumn is the season of falling, browning leaves, and the subject of Keats's ode To Autumn.

clue.text: Pig in dish — it may make one sick

indicators.note: the pig is placed inside the dish

parts.note: a paten is a shallow dish, used for the bread at communion
a hog is a pig

explanation.surface: A pig served in a dish that could make you ill.
explanation.definitionFit: A pathogen is a germ or microbe that causes disease, so something that makes one sick.

clue.text: National Park offering opportunity with traditional climbing

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the whole run reads upwards

parts.note: room, as in room for improvement, is scope or opportunity
trad is short for traditional

explanation.surface: A national park offers a chance to do some traditional rock climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns both pieces together: ROOM + TRAD read upwards gives DART + MOOR. 'Trad' is also a rock-climbing style, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Dartmoor is a national park of moorland in Devon, south-west England.

clue.text: Support exercise to treat about a stone

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

indicators.note: the word for treat goes around the abbreviation for stone

parts.note: to deal with something is to treat it
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight (14 lb)

explanation.surface: A support used for exercise sessions to deal with a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestal is the base or plinth that supports a statue or column.

clue.text: Party under deputy that is corrupt

indicators.note: in a down clue, the party sits under the deputy

parts.note: a rave is a lively party

explanation.surface: A party run by a deputy that turns out to be corrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: To deprave is to corrupt someone morally, a verb in both cases.

clue.text: Perhaps playing Strad that's deforming with age

definitions.meaning: drawing a bow across a violin such as a Stradivarius
bending or warping as wood or a back does over time

explanation.walkthrough: A Strad is a Stradivarius violin. The two senses are pronounced differently (bo- and bough-).
explanation.definitionFit: Bowing is both drawing a bow over strings and bending out of shape, as with an old shelf.

clue.text: Provide lift to where bells may be hung

definitions.meaning: to raise someone's spirits or encourage them
inside a church tower or steeple, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: To inspire is to uplift or motivate; read as two words it locates bells within a steeple.

clue.text: What might hold up breakfast?

parts.note: not something that delays the meal but a small holder that keeps a boiled egg upright

explanation.surface: Wondering what could be delaying the morning meal.
explanation.definitionFit: This small cup holds a boiled egg upright at the breakfast table.

clue.text: Snake biting head off insect

indicators.note: head off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a wasp is a stinging insect

explanation.surface: A snake bites the head off an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'biting' is a link that suits the snake picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An asp is a small venomous snake, the one said to have killed Cleopatra.

clue.text: Turn against one

indicators.note: turn signals that the following letters are turned into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone turns on a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition and the wordplay at once.
explanation.definitionFit: To antagonise someone is to make them hostile, turning them against you.

clue.text: Mass of material from half-completed garments

indicators.note: only the first half of the word for garments is finished, so the rest is cut off

parts.note: garments are clothes

explanation.surface: A heap of cloth left over from unfinished garments.
explanation.definitionFit: A clot is a thickened lump or mass, as of blood or cream.

clue.text: Young man receiving a medal is an unpopular person

indicators.note: receiving means the son takes in the letter A

parts.note: a son is a young male, someone's boy
DSO is the Distinguished Service Order, a British military decoration

explanation.surface: A young soldier being decorated turns out to be widely disliked.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a so-and-so is a mild euphemism for an unpleasant, disliked person.

clue.text: Oakley, maybe, taking tips off cigars of willing gents in rodeo line-up

indicators.note: the tips taken off are the first letters of each following word

explanation.surface: Annie Oakley takes the ends off the cigars of obliging men lined up at a rodeo.
explanation.walkthrough: Annie Oakley was a famous American sharpshooter of Wild West shows, so she is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Annie Oakley was a sharpshooting Wild West performer, an example of a cowgirl.

clue.text: Coming back with answer: time and space

indicators.note: coming back signals the word for time reads in reverse

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Returning with a reply about time and space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time and space' looks like a pair; 'and' is the link, so only space defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a region or expanse, a stretch of space.

clue.text: School work's certainly intended as sound early investment

parts.note: prep is school homework, a British public-school term

indicators.note: as sound says that the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: aye means certainly, yes, and meant means intended

explanation.surface: Homework done as a sound early investment in one's future.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective for the investment; it means the phrase 'aye meant' is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: A prepayment is money paid in advance, before it is due, so an early outlay.
